text:
Ashley (infra): Heads-up — saw a spike in pod Pending for gpu workloads this morning, 2min cold starts. Thinking warm pool for critical nodegroups.
Mike (sre): +1, numbers? which region/cluster?
Ashley (infra): eu-west-1 / eks-cluster-prod, ~15 pods Pending across 3 services. P95 scheduling latency ~120s.
Jun (platform): Are these all on the rtx-pool nodegroup? Was autoscaler scaling or we hit quota?
Ashley (infra): Mostly rtx-pool. Autoscaler did scale up but instances stalled at provisioning step (spot fallback to ondemand) so kubelet registration delayed.
Samira (eng): We should avoid apps timing out waiting for node readiness. Can we pre-create a tiny warm pool (1-2 nodes) with taints + tolerations and use Terraform to manage lifecycle?
Mike (sre): I prototyped something like that last week. Terraform creates an ASG with min=1, max=2, label node.kubernetes.io/warm=true and taint gpu-warm=true:NoSchedule. Then Helm values for autoscaler set expanderPolicy to more conservative.
Ashley (infra): Can you paste the snippet?
Mike (sre): Sure — terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_warm" {
  name = "eks-gpu-warm-\${var.env}"
  min_size = 1
  max_size = 2
  mixed_instances_policy { /* ... */ }
  tag { key = "node.kubernetes.io/warm" value = "true" propagate_at_launch = true }
}
```
Samira (eng): And Helm values to ensure CA ignores warm nodes? We need cluster-autoscaler not to evict or rely on them incorrectly.
Jun (platform): In our helmfile values: set `skipNodesWithLocalStorage=false` and add `ignoreDaemonsetsExclusion=true`? Actually we add a `--node-group-auto-discovery` filter to only match groups with `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled=true` label. Warm pool ASG should NOT have that label.
Mike (sre): Right — Helm values example:
```yaml
extraArgs:
  node-group-auto-discovery: "asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled,k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/${clusterName}"
  balance-similar-node-groups: true
```
This way warm ASG excluded unless we opt in.
Ashley (infra): Nice. How do we wire Terraform + Helmfile CI so warm pool created before we update autoscaler? Order matters to avoid transient spikes.
Jun (platform): In our pipeline we already have staged applies: 1) terraform apply nodegroups, 2) wait-for-nodes readiness (small script using `kubectl get nodes --selector=node.kubernetes.io/warm=true`), 3) helmfile apply cluster-autoscaler values. We can add a health-check gating step.
Samira (eng): Can we add lifecycle policy to keep at least 1 warm node on scale-in from ASG side? Spot interruptions were causing both warm nodes to go away simultaneously.
Mike (sre): Set ASG instance protection for the warm ASG during maintenance windows and use a different instance type spread across AZs. Also add a `creation_policy` in Terraform for a short cooldown.
Ashley (infra): Cost question — keeping 1-2 warm GPUs has steady cost. Estimated +$2k/month for eu-west small RTX instances. Is that acceptable for SLAs?
Samira (eng): For top-tier customers, yes. We can gate warm pools behind a feature flag per cluster/env.
Jun (platform): I'll draft a terraform module `gpu_warm_pool` and helmfile patch. Will post PRs.
autoscaler-bot: Deployment check: cluster-autoscaler helm release 'ca-prod' v1.6.3 is healthy in eu-west-1.
Ashley (infra): Thanks — next steps: Jun to PR terraform module, Samira to add toleration/taint docs for app owners, Mike to add pipeline gating script. If anyone sees pod Pending again, ping #oncall. :bell:
